paragraphs: The reading list this talk stands on. Call out a couple of pairings: Newman's Building Microservices for the boundaries and integration story; Kleppmann's Designing Data-Intensive Applications for the data and consistency foundations behind the outbox and saga; Bellemare for the event-driven backbone; and the API-design trio (Higginbotham, Zimmermann et al., Geewax) for contract and versioning depth. The architecture books are language-agnostic — they apply whether you build on Quarkus, Spring or anything else. The Quarkus guides plus the Quarkus Flow and Debezium docs are the practical references for the runtime specifics shown in the code. The slides and these references are enough to build the system, not only to discuss it. The full list, with a publisher link for every title, is on the site's Bibliography page (patterncatalyst.github.io/cloud-native-design-patterns/bibliography/).
